comparison_vs_phase_c3_postfix.notes: Final run matches Phase C.3 post-fix steady-state within noise (<6% absolute drift on per-op latencies). Wall-clock improved 17% due to no first-call npx cache miss (the prior pipeline left the npx cache warm). Confirms the C.3 lazy-init optimization is stable across runs and the graphAdapter retirement did not regress any metric.

gate_decision.rule: Per ADR-0170 §'Performance benchmark gate': no >10% regression vs SQLite baseline on any of (store p50, store p95, search p50, search p95, total wall). Speedup is acceptable; the rule is about slowdowns.
gate_decision.narrative: Every metric is a SPEEDUP vs the SQLite baseline. The C.3 lazy ControllerRegistry init (memory_*-axis routes no longer pay agentdb_* substrate cost) accounts for ~24-43% of the per-op improvement; the Phase D dead-code stripping (sqlite-vec, hnswlib, graph-node, GraphDatabaseAdapter) accounts for the remaining tail. Memory consumption (rss_peak_bytes captured at the bench-process level, not the spawned CLI) is informational only — the bench's RSS-capture bug from gap-K is still present (~54KB reported is the bench wrapper's own RSS, not the spawnSync child's). Per `feedback-no-squelch-tests` the 10% band was NOT widened. Per `feedback-no-fallbacks` lazy init preserves loud-fail semantics — the agentdb_*-axis path still throws ADR-0165 markers if the substrate is unreachable on first agentdb_* tool call.
